generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology this runs through everything from a lab report to an essay on theory. Before writing, you remind yourself how psychology hedges its claims, reports method precisely, and ties conclusions to evidence. As you draft, you bring studies in to support your argument and show where you are weighing them, not just listing them. Each assignment sharpens your sense of what the field expects next time.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students write up the same study for a module. One uses an everyday, chatty style and simply states that the study 'proves' the theory. The other has read widely in the field, matches its cautious, evidence-tied style, and uses the study to support a carefully qualified claim of her own. The second write-up reads like psychology, because she has recognised the conventions, learned them from her reading, and put them to work in one move.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, writing as a member of the field is a continuing practice. You recognise its conventions, learn them by reading studies and reviews as a writer, and integrate sources with a critical edge so your own argument leads. Done on every assignment, it is what makes your writing read as psychology rather than as general prose.

check.body: A student notices that history essays argue in the writer's own voice, reads several to confirm it, then drafts a paragraph that opens in her own voice and uses a source to support her point. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That she is running the three strands as one practice: recognising a convention, confirming it by reading, then writing to it with a critical edge.
_items.feedback: Yes. She moved through all three strands, one after another, as one connected practice.

_items.text: That she has memorised a set of rules that apply to every subject.
_items.feedback: The conventions she used belong to history, not to every subject.

_items.text: That reading published work replaces the need to write anything of her own.
_items.feedback: She still wrote her own paragraph; reading informed it rather than replacing it.

_items.text: That recognising a convention is all that matters, and the drafting is optional.
_items.feedback: Recognising the convention was only the first strand; she then read and drafted too.
